We currently have a permanent role available within our Investments Department for an Asset Servicing Senior Administrator.  The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring investment transactions are processed and accurately reflected on client policies following trade execution, helping to maintain accurate valuations and a seamless experience for policyholders and advisers.

Reporting to the Asset Servicing Team Manager, the key responsibilities of the role include:

Manage dividend processing activities, ensuring investment data is maintained accurately and in line with operational controls.
Oversee trade settlement activities, resolve exceptions and support the timely completion of market transactions, including complex cross-border settlements.
Administer corporate actions from notification through to completion, preparing communications and processing customer and adviser instructions accurately and efficiently.
Deliver excellent service to advisers, clients and colleagues by managing queries professionally and ensuring timely resolution of issues.
Maintain and update asset records, taking ownership of data quality and supporting the effective administration of investment assets.
Investigate and resolve reconciliation discrepancies, working with custodians and internal stakeholders to maintain accurate financial records. 
Support the monitoring and reconciliation of investment cash positions, identifying and resolving queries to ensure data integrity.
Support the Asset Servicing Team Manager with process, procedure and system improvements that enhance operational efficiency and control.

To be successful in this role, candidates should possess the following skills and experience:

Experience within an operational, settlements, reconciliation or corporate-action environment
5 GCSEs (or equivalent) grade C or above - including English and Maths
Strong numeracy, accuracy and attention to detail
Ability to work effectively under pressure and manage competing deadlines
Good planning and organisational skills
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
Certificate or interest in studying for CISI examinations is advantageous
Previous experience supporting junior colleagues or acting as a process reference point would be beneficial

We encourage and welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds because we embrace diversity and inclusivity within our business.
If you, or you know someone who is interested in applying for this position, please forward a current CV with a covering letter to careers@ifg-ltd.com 
Closing date for this vacancy will be 7 August 2026.

In this role, you will support the delivery of business-as-usual activity across Finance, help maintain system integrity, manage finance system processes and user access, and contribute to finance and Group-wide projects. You will work closely with colleagues across the business to resolve queries, support systems administration, and identify opportunities to improve the way Finance operates.

The main duties for the role holder will include:
Provide day-to-day support to the Finance function, including user access, chart of accounts updates and general finance system queries.
Take a lead role in the administration of the Group purchase order system, including system set-up, authorisation hierarchies and process improvements.
Support the bespoke Finance Data Hub solution and help ensure finance data remains accurate, accessible and well controlled.
Contribute to finance-specific and Group-wide projects, including requirements gathering, development, testing and implementation activity.
Review existing finance processes and systems, making recommendations that improve efficiency, control and user experience.
Support the implementation and upgrade of accounting systems, controls and procedures.
Assist with the reconciliation of system control accounts, analysing results, liaising with stakeholders and supporting corrective action where needed.

We're looking for an experienced and motivated fitness coach to join the team at FitBody Fitness, delivering high-quality small group personal training sessions to our members. The main focus of the role is coaching small groups through structured, progressive programming, making sure every client trains safely, stays motivated and keeps moving towards their goals session after session. You'll also be responsible for inducting new members, taking them through their initial assessments and helping them settle in so they feel confident and supported from day one. Just as important is the work that happens between sessions, with regular check-ins to keep clients accountable on their training, nutrition and lifestyle, building the kind of relationships that keep people engaged and coming back. The ideal candidate holds a recognised Level 3 personal training qualification, has genuine experience coaching groups rather than only one-to-one, and brings the energy, reliability and communication skills needed to lead a room full of different abilities. You'll need to be organised, personable and genuinely invested in getting results for the people you coach. To apply, send your CV along with a short note about your coaching experience and why you'd be a good fit for FitBody Fitness to Darren@fitbodyfitness.im@hotmail.com

You will provide on-site expertise on specialist equipment such as the CEMs (Emissions monitoring) and DCS/PLCs. You should also provide cross functional support to other team members, as and when required.
Supporting the installation, testing, commissioning and modification of plant equipment, ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and engineering standards.

Completed relevant engineering apprenticeship and qualified to City & Guilds or NVQ Level 3 (or equivalent).
Knowledge of wiring regulations BS7671 (18th edition).

We are recruiting for an Assistant Chief Officer (Environment) to join the Environment & Regeneration Department to support and participate in the overall leadership of the Department.  The postholder will support the Director of Environment & Regeneration and will lead, plan and control the operation and staff of the Environment Section which includes Fleet Services & Stores, Waste Services, and Electrical Services and Engineering.  You will be the Council’s lead officer on construction/civil projects and will also be the Premises Manager for the Operational depot. 

Applicants must have extensive experience of construction/civil/engineering development either within the public or private sector.  Prior knowledge and experience of how corporate and support teams are established and operated is essential particularly in relation to strategy and communication.  Applicants will also need to be able to demonstrate senior leadership experience at Head of Department/Service level or equivalent.  We are looking for a senior leader who can drive the operation forward, think strategically and influence change whilst inspiring colleagues through clear communication.  

You must be a highly motivated self-starter and resilient with strong interpersonal and communication skills and have the ability to interface with all levels.  Solid stakeholder management, relationship building and influencing skills are a must as well as excellent organisational, technical, analytical and program and project management skills.  You must also have the ability to think strategically and be able to identify core issues and potential solution strategies in this demanding role.  

As a key member of the Department’s Senior Management Team, and a member of the Extended Chief Officers’ Management Team, the role is a vital part of the Department and of the Council as a whole in supporting the effective leadership of the organisation.  Delivering services in a sustainable way will be a key emphasis of this role, supporting the whole Council in achieving its low carbon ambitions and delivery of the Corporate Plan.

If you have substantial experience and success in managing at a senior level and can demonstrate a track record of delivery of high quality services within either the public or private sectors then we would like to hear from you!  

For an informal discussion about the position, please email khiggins@douglas.gov.im in order to arrange a call with Iain Jackson, Director of Environment & Regeneration.  

Application form and job description: downloaded at www.douglas.im.  Closing date for submission of completed applications is Friday, 14th August 2026.

We are recruiting for an Assistant Chief Officer (Environment) to join the Environment & Regeneration Department to support and participate in the overall leadership of the Department.  The postholder will support the Director of Environment & Regeneration and will lead, plan and control the operation and staff of the Environment Section which includes Fleet Services & Stores, Waste Services, and Electrical Services and Engineering.  You will be the Council’s lead officer on construction/civil projects and will also be the Premises Manager for the Operational depot. 

Applicants must have extensive experience of construction/civil/engineering development either within the public or private sector.  Prior knowledge and experience of how corporate and support teams are established and operated is essential particularly in relation to strategy and communication.  Applicants will also need to be able to demonstrate senior leadership experience at Head of Department/Service level or equivalent.  We are looking for a senior leader who can drive the operation forward, think strategically and influence change whilst inspiring colleagues through clear communication.  

You must be a highly motivated self-starter and resilient with strong interpersonal and communication skills and have the ability to interface with all levels.  Solid stakeholder management, relationship building and influencing skills are a must as well as excellent organisational, technical, analytical and program and project management skills.  You must also have the ability to think strategically and be able to identify core issues and potential solution strategies in this demanding role.  

As a key member of the Department’s Senior Management Team, and a member of the Extended Chief Officers’ Management Team, the role is a vital part of the Department and of the Council as a whole in supporting the effective leadership of the organisation.  Delivering services in a sustainable way will be a key emphasis of this role, supporting the whole Council in achieving its low carbon ambitions and delivery of the Corporate Plan.

If you have substantial experience and success in managing at a senior level and can demonstrate a track record of delivery of high quality services within either the public or private sectors then we would like to hear from you!  

For an informal discussion about the position, please email khiggins@douglas.gov.im in order to arrange a call with Iain Jackson, Director of Environment & Regeneration.

Act as a key legal contact for business stakeholders, providing clear, pragmatic, and commercially focused advice. Take ownership of legal support for designated business areas. Ability to work independently, take ownership, and manage priorities. Experience improving legal processes, templates, or ways of working is highly desirable. Excellent drafting, negotiation, and communication skills. Ability to provide practical, business-focused advice in a clear and concise manner. Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work effectively across different jurisdictions and cultures. A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset and interest in the gaming/technology space. Experience working with legal technology tools (e.g. CLM systems, document automation) is advantageous. Notes
Bidvest Noonan is seeking reliable and professional Casual Security Officers to join our team at the Isle of Man Courts of Justice. This is a zero-hour contract position, providing cover on an as-required basis, making it ideal for individuals seeking flexible work opportunities.
About the Role
Working within a secure and professional environment, you will play a vital role in maintaining the safety and security of the Courts of Justice building, its staff, visitors, and users.
Using an airport-style security screening approach, your duties will include:
Monitoring access points to the Courts of Justice building.
Conducting security searches of persons and property before authorising entry.
Carrying out regular internal and external foot patrols.
Monitoring visitor numbers and maintaining accurate records and reports.
Operating and monitoring the building's CCTV systems.
Identifying and responding appropriately to disruptive or escalating behaviour.
Providing excellent customer service whilst maintaining a safe and secure environment.
Developing positive working relationships with court staff, service users, and our client.
What We're Looking For
The successful candidate will be:
Professional, reliable, and trustworthy.
Calm and patient under pressure.
An excellent communicator with strong interpersonal skills.
Confident dealing with members of the public.
Flexible and available to work shifts at short notice when required.
Able to work independently and as part of a wider team.
Previous security experience is desirable but not essential, as full training will be provided.
Training
Successful candidates will receive comprehensive training, including:
Emergency First Aid at Work.
Automated External Defibrillation (AED).
Conflict Management and De-escalation.
Fire Marshal Training.
Control and Restraint.
Working Pattern
Casual 0-hour contract.
Monday to Friday shifts available as required.
Weekend on-call opportunities available.
Hours offered according to operational needs and cover requirements.
How to Apply
To apply, please submit your CV and a brief covering letter.
For further information, please contact:
Liam Otten 
Email: Liam.Otten@bidvestnoonan.com
Telephone: 01624 685264
Bidvest Noonan is committed to providing equal opportunities and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates.

Notes
Car Sales Executive – Full Time.

Manx Car Store is a highly respected, family?run used car dealership on the Isle of Man, known for offering an exceptional range of vehicles—from reliable family cars to premium high?performance models. Due to continued growth, we are seeking a motivated and professional Car Sales Executive to join our successful team.

About the Role:
We are looking for a proactive, confident individual with a strong background in sales. Previous experience within the motor trade or car sales is highly preferred; however, we are also open to candidates with solid general sales experience who are excellent on the phone, strong face?to?face with customers, and driven to succeed. The ideal candidate will be articulate, IT?literate, well?presented, and able to deliver outstanding customer service at every stage of the sales process.

Key responsibilities include, Providing exceptional customer service and maintain a professional, welcoming showroom environment, build trust and rapport with customers through face?to?face, phone, and digital communication, maintain strong product knowledge of current stock and incoming vehicles, conduct vehicle test drives and accurately evaluate part exchanges, consistently achieve and exceed sales targets while upholding high customer care standards, ensure vehicles are fully prepared and ready for customer handover. advise customers on suitable finance options, warranties, and accessories, assist with website management, marketing activities, and uploading new stock, manage customer enquiries pre? and post?sale with professionalism and efficiency, work collaboratively with colleagues to maintain a positive, high?performing sales environment.

Experience & Skills Required:
1–2 years sales experience (motor trade experience strongly preferred).
Confident communicator with excellent phone and face?to?face customer skills.
Highly motivated, target?driven, and able to work independently.
Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
IT literate and comfortable using CRM systems and online platforms.
A genuine people person with a positive, professional attitude.
Minimum age 21 with a clean full UK driving licence (insurance requirement).

How to Apply:
Please email your CV to: tony.dhadwal@manxcarstore.com / sharne.bradley@manxcarstore.com

Van Mossel Jacksons are looking for an experienced Brand Manager in premium sales of motor vehicles (BYD & Volvo) to join their dedicated team. Working within Jacksons you will be skilled and seasoned Brand Manager in the sales of our current brands of premium new and preowned vehicles.

**Some of the responsibilities for the Brand Manager position are, but not limited to;**

Engage in the art of following up with both loyal and potential customers, nurturing relationships to bring about further transactions. 
Strive to meet and exceed monthly targets for the sale of both new and used cars. 
Seek out and approach new clients with steadfast determination, arranging meetings to understand and address their needs.
Achieve monthly sales targets for New and Used vehicles, achieving the minimum profit targets.
Achieve monthly sales targets for additional profit centres including finance.
Return correspondence from customers and ensure all matters of paperwork are tended to with diligence.
Seize every opportunity to maximise sales whilst ensuring complete customer satisfaction.

**The Brand Manager position comes with an excellent remuneration and other benefits;**

Starting Salary & excellent bonus scheme
Guaranteed Income: A generous sum guaranteed for the first three months as you train and settle in the new role.
Company Car: A desirable chariot. 
Training and Accreditation: To make sure you are developed to reach the highest level of commission.

**Requirements:**
You must possess experience in the sales, a requirement without compromise.
Knowledge of the Kerridge/ADP DMS system a benefit.
The gift of clear communication, both by phone and in person, is essential.
A valid Driving Licence.
Highly presentable, ambitious and target driven, you will have a strong passion for car sales in order to meet and exceed agreed targets for the sale of vehicles and related products.

For more details and to apply contact recruitment@jacksons.je

Notes
Be part of something precise, impactful, and innovative.
Are you someone who enjoys hands-on work, thrives in a laboratory environment, and takes pride in doing things with accuracy and care? We’re looking for a Production Technician to join our team and play a key role in manufacturing high-quality chromatography products that support important scientific and commercial outcomes.
This is more than just a production role — it’s an opportunity to contribute to continuous improvement, process optimisation, and innovation in a regulated, high-performing environment.

What you’ll be doing - You’ll be at the heart of our manufacturing operations, helping ensure our products are produced safely, efficiently, and to the highest standards. Your responsibilities will include: Manufacturing chromatography products, intermediates, and base materials, Following established SOPs and production methods with precision, Recording production data accurately and maintaining detailed documentation, Carrying out on-line quality control checks and identifying any anomalies early, Supporting process optimisation and improvement initiatives, Maintaining equipment and ensuring a clean, safe working environment
You’ll also contribute to: Improving processes and maximising yields, Writing and updating SOPs and production methods, Sharing knowledge and supporting the development of colleagues
We’re looking for someone who is practical, detail-focused, and proactive, with a genuine interest in laboratory-based manufacturing.
You’ll thrive in this role if you are: A strong team player with good communication skills, Highly organised with excellent attention to detail, Comfortable working both independently and as part of a team, A natural problem solver who can spot issues early, Able to follow processes accurately while also contributing ideas for improvement
Desirable experience: A-levels or degree in a scientific discipline, Experience in regulated manufacturing (ideally chemical or similar environments) Familiarity with laboratory equipment and processes
This is a hands-on, laboratory-based role where no two days are quite the same. You can expect: A physically active role involving standing, lifting, and equipment operation, A structured environment with a strong focus on quality and safety, 24/7 shift patterns supporting continuous operations
You’ll be part of a collaborative team where your contribution directly impacts product quality, operational success, and continuous improvement. We value curiosity, precision, and teamwork — and we’re always looking for ways to do things better.
If you’re looking for a role where you can build your skills, contribute to meaningful work, and be part of a supportive and driven team, we’d love to hear from you. Please apply using the following link - https://biotage-1708019070.teamtailor.com/jobs/8139650-production-chemist-astrea
